text:
Sam: Heads up — running the new minimal Next 13 starter (edge runtime) with the LangChain sample and the eval harness, seeing duplicate completions when the SDK retries. Anyone else hit this?
Maya: yep saw that today in my local smoke tests. looks like the SDK retry kicks in after a streaming disconnect and the harness treats both chunks as final completions.
Dmitri: can you paste the call pattern? is this the hosted API or a Private deployment?
Sam: hosted for me (dev account). call pattern: client.chat.completions.stream with an async for -> we append to buffer then on complete we emit to eval. snippet:```js
const stream = await client.chat.completions.stream({ model: 'redwood-4x', input, retry: { enabled: true } });
let buf = '';
for await (const part of stream) { buf += part.delta; }
emitEvalResult(buf);```
Sam: logs show two finalization events:```
[I 12:00:01] stream closed, code=1006
[I 12:00:01] retrying request (id=abc123)
[I 12:00:02] final completion id=abc123, tokens=120
[I 12:00:02] final completion id=abc123-retry, tokens=119
```
Maya: interesting, looks like the retry path is creating a new completion id but our harness dedupe relies on original id. if the retry creates a different id the harness can't tell.
Dmitri: two angles — (1) SDK should expose an idempotency key or propagate original request id onto retries, (2) eval harness should treat proxied stream reconnects as continuation rather than separate run.
Sam: as a quick workaround I disabled retry in the client config and re-ran, duplicates went away. Not ideal for flaky networks.
Maya: @Dmitri could we make the SDK keep a stable request id across retries? maybe add `x-redwood-original-id` header or a `meta.request_id` field on the stream events.
Dmitri: yeah that's feasible. we need to be careful with streaming libs because resuming is weird. I'll prototype: keep a static request_id per high-level call and include it in both events and retry attempts.
Sam: also saw this interaction with Next's Edge SSR — the edge runtime killed the connection on cold starts which triggers a retry and creates duplicate eval entries.
Maya: could add a small debounce in the eval harness: if two completions for same request_id arrive within 500ms mark as duplicate. low impact and buys time until SDK fix.
Sam: filing a minimal repro repo now. includes Next 13 minimal app, langchain wiring, and the eval harness script. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devx-repros/next-eval-dup (private)
Dmitri: thanks. I'll open a patch PR to SDK: add stable request_id + include it in stream close/retry events. assign to me.
Maya: created an eval-harness PR that does the 500ms dedupe and respects `meta.request_id` when present. PR: https://git.internal/r/devx/eval-harness/pulls/42
Sam: repro attached: stack + logs + small test. run with `yarn start && node scripts/run-eval.js --sample next-minimal`
DX Bot: FYI — added the repro ticket to sprint board: DEVEX-814
ci-bot: build passed for branch sdk/stable-reqid (commit 9f8a7b) — https://ci.redwood.ai/blue/organizations/jenkins/sdk/detail/sdk%2Fstable-reqid/1/pipeline
Dmitri: opened draft PR for SDK: https://git.internal/r/sdk/pulls/167 — adds stable request id, injects header, emits meta.request_id on stream events. leaving as draft until tests.
Sam: awesome. after SDK PR merges we'll flip on retries in the starter and re-run the eval harness.
Maya: note for docs: mention Edge runtime connection fragility + recommended retry semantics + how to opt into stable request ids. I'll draft a small doc blurb if you want.
Dmitri: please do. I'll add integration tests that simulate a stream disconnect and ensure the harness doesn't double-count.
Sam: thanks all — good cross-team sync. tagging followups: @Maya for docs, @Dmitri for SDK PR, @Sam for repro cleanup. :thumbsup:
